topics.title: Dangers of Neglecting the Hair | Ways of Caring for the Hair Primary 1 (Basic 1) - Home Economics
topics.content:
HOME ECONOMICS
PREVOCATIONAL STUDIES
SECOND TERM
WEEK 3
PRIMARY 1
THEME - GROOMING
PREVIOUS LESSON - Care of the Hair - Hair Care Materials and Tools Primary 1 (Basic 1) - Home Economics
TOPIC - CARE OF THE HAIR
LEARNING AREA
1. Introductory Activities
2. Ways of Caring Materials and Tools
3. Dangers of Dirty Hair (Dangers of Neglecting the Hair)
4. Lesson Evaluation and Weekly Assessment (Test)
PERFORMANCE OBJECTIVES
By the end of the lesson, most the pupils should have attained the following objectives (cognitive, affective and psychomotor) and should be able to -
1. state the dangers of wearing dirty hair.
2. state the ways of caring for the hair.
3. keep their hair clean and tidy.
4. Lesson Evaluation and Weekly Assessment (Test)
ENTRY BEHAVIOUR
The pupils know how to comb and apply hair cream to their hair.
INSTRUCTIONAL MATERIALS
The teacher will teach the lesson with the aid of:
Display of hair care materials and tools such as bowls, soaps, water, comb, brush, towel, hair cream/pomade.
METHOD OF TEACHING
Choose a suitable and appropriate methods for the lessons.
Note - Irrespective of choosing methods of teaching, always introduce an activities that will arouse pupil’s interest or lead them to the lessons.
REFERENCE MATERIALS
1. Scheme of Work
2. 9 - Years Basic Education Curriculum
3. Course Book
4. All Relevant Material
5. Online Information
WRITING INSTRUCTION
Copy as I write or draw as I write. This instruction should be given when you need the pupils to write or draw.
CONTENT OF THE LESSON
LESSON 1 - INTRODUCTORY ACTIVITIES
Teacher’s Activities - Display charts showing clean hair diseases for the pupils discuss and state some of the hair diseases.
Pupil’s Activities - Active participation in the class discussion.
Teacher’s remark - The charts shown the danger of dirty hair or neglecting your hair. Did you want to hair to be like one of these? If no, you must take care of your hair.
Based on the previous assignment - Care of the Hair - Hair Care Materials and Tools Primary 1 (Basic 1) - Home Economics, ask pupils - what are the danger of dirt hair? Support with reference to the chart and write their points on the board.
DANGERS OF NEGLECTING THE HAIR
The following are danger of dirty hair -
1. Lice
2. Dandruff
3. Ringworm
4. Overgrown
5. Untidy hair, etc.
LESSON 2 - CARING FOR THE HAIR
Teacher’s/Pupil’s Activities - Lead the pupils to discuss ways of taking care of the hair by the boys and girl.
WAYS OF CARING FOR HAIR FOR THE BOYS
1. Avoid playing with sand.
2. Cut your hair when overgrown.
3. Wash your hair regularly.
4. Always use clean towel after washing.
5. Apply hair cream or pomade.
6. Avoid playing with sand.
7. Always use clean towel after washing.
8. Comb or brush regularly.
WAYS OF CARING FOR HAIR FOR THE GIRLS
1. Cut your hair low, otherwise do the following -
2. Comb regularly
3. Wash your hair regularly.
4. Apply the appropriate pomade.
5. Plait or weave your hair on Weekly or monthly basis (depending on the type of hair style).
6. Cover your hair.
7. Avoid playing with sand.
ASSIGNMENT
Find out the uses of ears and nose.
PRESENTATION
To deliver the lesson, the teacher adopts the following steps:
1. To introduce the lesson, the teacher revises the previous lesson. Based on this, he/she asks the pupils some questions;
2. Displays charts showing clean hair diseases for the pupils discuss and state some of the hair diseases.
Pupil’s Activities - Participate actively in the class discussion.
3. Leads pupils to discuss ways of taking care of the hair by the boys and girl.
Pupil’s Activities - Follow the teacher’s lead and state some of the ways to care for hair.
4. Summarizes the lesson on the board.
Pupil’s Activities - Copy as the teacher writes.
CONCLUSION
To conclude the lesson for the week, the teacher revises the entire lesson and links it to the following week’s lesson.
NEXT LESSON
Functions of the Ears and Nose | Materials for Cleaning the Ears and the Nose Primary 1 (Basic 1) - Home Economics
LESSON EVALUATION
Ask pupils to:
1. mention two hair care materials and tools.
2. list two ways to keep the hair clean.
3. mention two dangers of keeping dirty hair.
WEEKLY ASSESSMENT
ATTEMPT ALL THE QUESTIONS
1. ____________ and ____________ should be avoid playing with sand.
A. Boys and males
B. Girls and females
C. Boys and girls
2. ____________ must plait their hair regularly.
A. Boys
B. Girls
C. Males
3. Cutting of hair is common among the ____________.
A. boys
B. girls
C. female
4. It is not a must to cut the hair for ____________.
A. boys
B. girls
C. Males
5. ____________ and ____________ must wash their hair regularly.
A. boys and males
B. girls and females
C. boys and girls
6. ____________ is one of the dangers of dirty hair.
A. Lice
B. Rat
C. Bird
State 4 dangers of dirty hair.
7. ____________
8. ____________
9. ____________
10. ____________

topics.title: Functions of the Eyes | Materials for the Care of the Eyes | Dangers of not Caring for the Eyes Primary 1 (Basic 1) - Home Economics
topics.content:
HOME ECONOMICS
PREVOCATIONAL STUDIES
SECOND TERM
WEEK 7
PRIMARY 1
THEME - GROOMING
PREVIOUS LESSON - Dangers of not Caring for the Ears and Nose Primary 1 (Basic 1) - Home Economics
TOPIC -THE EYES
LEARNING AREA
1. Introductory Activities
2. Identification of the Eyes
3. Functions of the Eyes
3. Materials for Cleaning the Eyes
4. Dangers of not Caring for the Eyes
5. Lesson Evaluation and Weekly Assessment (Test)
PERFORMANCE OBJECTIVES
By the end of the lesson, the pupils should have attained the following objectives (cognitive, affective and psychomotor) and should be able to -
1. identify the eyes.
2. state the functions of the eyes.
3. list the materials for cleaning the eyes.
4. take care of their eyes.
ENTRY BEHAVIOUR
The pupils can point to their eyes and state their uses.
INSTRUCTIONAL MATERIALS
The teacher will teach the lesson with the aid of:
1. Chart showing the eyes.
2. Materials and tools for caring for the eyes.
METHOD OF TEACHING
Choose a suitable and appropriate methods for the lessons.
Note - Irrespective of choosing methods of teaching, always introduce an activities that will arouse pupil’s interest or lead them to the lessons.
REFERENCE MATERIALS
1. Scheme of Work
2. 9 - Years Basic Education Curriculum
3. Course Book
4. All Relevant Material
5. Online Information
WRITING INSTRUCTION
Copy as I write or draw as I write. This instruction should be given when you need the pupils to write or draw.
CONTENT OF THE LESSON
LESSON 1 - INTRODUCTORY QUESTIONS - FUNCTIONS OF THE EYES
Teacher’s Activities - Asks the pupils,
1. The parts of the body that’s used for seeing is _________.
2. Point to your eyes.
3. Everybody close your eyes, what did you see?
4. Open your eyes and mention 5 things that you see in the class.
Pupil’s Activities - Response to questions,
1. Eyes
2. This is my eyes.
3. Nothing
4. Chair, tables, board, board, etc.
Teacher’s remarks - Our eyes are parts of the body that’s used for seeing. We can see one another and things with around. We need to take care our eyes from time to time. Display chart showing materials used for caring for the eyes for the pupils to identify and discuss. Note the materials on the board.
MATERIALS NEEDED FOR THE CARE OF THE EYES
The following are materials used for caring for our eyes -
1. Sunglasses
2. Face cap
3. Umbrella
4. Eyes drop
5. Healthy food
LESSON 2 - INTRODUCTORY ACTIVITIES
Teacher’s Activities - Display chart showing some of eye’s problems for the pupils to examine and identify different eye’s problems.
Pupil’s Activities - Active participation.
Teacher’s remark - Comment and discuss the dangers of not caring for the eyes.
QUICK EVALUATION
1. What is main function of the eyes?
2. State 3 materials needed for the care of the eyes.
DANGERS OF NOT CARING FOR THE EYES
The following are the dangers of not caring for the eyes -
1. Blindness
2. Weak vision
3. Short sight
4. Eyes pain
5. Double vision
6. Change colour
7. Unusual discharge or tear
8. Itching
QUICK EVALUATION
Mention 3 dangers of not caring for the eyes.
ASSIGNMENT
Find out ways of caring for the eyes.
PRESENTATION
To deliver the lesson, the teacher adopts the following steps:
1. To introduce the lesson, the teacher revises the previous lesson. Based on this, he/she asks the pupils some questions;
2. Displays chart of the eyes.
Pupil’s Activities - Identify the eyes.
3. Leads pupils to state some of the materials used for caring for the eyes.
Pupil’s Activities - State some of the materials used for caring for the eyes.
4. Discuss the dangers of not taking care of the eyes.
Pupil’s Activities - Dangers of not taking care of the eyes.
5. Summarizes the lesson on the board.
Pupil’s Activities - Copy as the teacher writes.
CONCLUSION
To conclude the lesson for the week, the teacher revises the entire lesson and links it to the following week’s lesson.
NEXT LESSON
Care of the Eyes - Ways of Caring for the Eyes Primary 1 (Basic 1) - Home Economics
LESSON EVALUATION
Ask pupils to:
1. draw their eyes from the chart shown.
2. mention three functions of the eyes.
WORKBOOK WEEKLY
ASSESSMENT (TEST)
1. ______________ are parts of the body used for seeing.
A. Eyes
B. Ears
C. Nose
2. We ______________ eyes.
A. 2
B. Two
C. 2 (two)
3. We can’t see everything when we close our eyes.
A. Yes
B. No
4. Good food improves our eyes ______________.
A. Vision
B. Blindness
C. Eyes pain
5. ______________ is not one of the dangers of not caring for the eyes.
A. Seeing
B. Vision
C. Blindness
State 3 materials needed for the care of the eyes.
6. ______________
7. ______________
8. ______________
Mention 2 dangers of not caring for the eyes.
9. ______________
10. ______________

Pupil’s Activities - This is the father, mother and their children.
Note - Accept home or house as place where they live.
Teacher’s remark - Everyone has a family and home where they live. Write the meaning of home on the board as discussed.
MEANING OF HOME
Home is a place (house) where people live as a family.
At home, we are safe because all members of the family loved one another.
We are protected from dangerous animals and bad weather.
LESSON 2 - REPEAT THE ACTIVITIES IN LESSON 1

1. To introduce the lesson, the teacher revises the previous lesson. Based on this, he/she asks the pupils some questions;
2. Leads pupils to identify home as a place where people live as a family.
Pupil’s Activities - Identify home as a place where people live as a family.
3. Summarizes the lesson on the board.
Pupil’s Activities - Copy as the teacher writes.

HOME ECONOMICS
PREVOCATIONAL STUDIES
SECOND TERM
WEEK 10
PRIMARY 1
THEME - GROOMING
PREVIOUS LESSON - Meaning of Home Primary 1 (Basic 1) - Home Economics
TOPIC - THE HOME
LEARNING AREA
1. Introductory Activities
2. Meaning of Home
3. Parts of A Home
4. Uses of Each Parts of A Home
5. Revision and Weekly Assessment (Test)
PERFORMANCE OBJECTIVES
By the end of the lesson, the pupils should have attained the following objectives (cognitive, affective and psychomotor) and should be able to -
1. explain the meaning of a home.
2. name the different parts of a home.
3. state uses of each part of a home.
ENTRY BEHAVIOUR
The pupils can identify and explain the meaning of home.
INSTRUCTIONAL MATERIALS
The teacher will teach the lesson with the aid of:
1. A picture of a home.
2. A chart showing different parts of the home.
METHOD OF TEACHING
Choose a suitable and appropriate methods for the lessons.
Note - Irrespective of choosing methods of teaching, always introduce an activities that will arouse pupil’s interest or lead them to the lessons.
REFERENCE MATERIALS
1. Scheme of Work
2. 9 - Years Basic Education Curriculum
3. Course Book
4. All Relevant Material
5. Online Information
WRITING INSTRUCTION
Copy as I write or draw as I write. This instruction should be given when you need the pupils to write or draw.
CONTENT OF THE LESSON
LESSON 1 - INTRODUCTORY ACTIVITIES
Teacher’s Activities - Take the pupils to the nearest teacher’s or parent’s home (on visitation or permission) for the pupils to identify different parts of the home and discuss their uses. OR Display charts showing different parts of a home for pupils to identify the parts of the home.
Pupil’s Responses - This is the parlour (sitting room), bedroom, etc.
Teacher’s remark - Home is a place (house) where people live as a family. There are different parts of home (as the pupils mentioned) with different uses. Write on board different parts of home and their uses as identity and discussed by the pupils.
MEANING OF HOME
Home a house or apartment where people lives as a family.
DIFFERENT PARTS OF A HOME AND THEIR USES
1. Bedrooms
2. Sitting (Living) room, commonly called parlour.
3. Bathrooms
4. Toilets
5. Kitchen
6. Dining room
7. Store
LESSON 2 - USES OF DIFFERENT PARTS OF A HOME AND THEIR USES
1. Bedroom
- The bedroom is where we sleep.
2. Sitting/living room
- The sitting or living is where we welcome (entertain) visitors and relax.
3. Bathroom
- The bathroom is where we have our bath.
4. Toilet
- The toilet is where we pass out waste product from the body.
5. Kitchen
- The kitchen is where we cook.
6. Dining
- The dining room is where we eat our food.
7. Store
- The store is where we keep our foodstuff, kitchen equipments and other things.
QUICK ASSESSMENT
Ask pupils to name 3 different parts of a home and their uses.
ASSIGNMENT
Find out the items found in -
1. Sitting/living room -
2. Bedrooms -
3. Bathroom -
4. Toilet -
5. Kitchen -
6. Store -
PRESENTATION
To deliver the lesson, the teacher adopts the following steps:
1. To introduce the lesson, the teacher revises the previous lesson. Based on this, he/she asks the pupils some questions;
2. Asks pupils to state different parts of the home and their uses.
Pupil’s Activities - Identify and state the uses of different parts of the home.
3. Summarizes the lesson on the board.
Pupil’s Activities - Copy as the teacher writes.
CONCLUSION
To conclude the lesson for the week, the teacher revises the entire lesson and links it to the following week’s lesson.
